content: Ongoing research is being conducted to understand the effects of glucose-lowering medications on COVID-19 outcomes in individuals with diabetes. Preliminary studies have yielded mixed results, with some glucose-lowering drugs potentially influencing inflammation or immune responses, which could, in turn, affect infection outcomes. However, despite these investigations, no conclusive evidence has been established to confirm the benefits of specific glucose-lowering medications in either preventing or treating COVID-19. As a result, the primary focus remains on vaccinating individuals with diabetes to reduce their risk of severe complications associated with COVID-19. Healthcare providers are advised to tailor diabetes management strategies to minimize risks, particularly for older adults and those with long-standing diabetes, as these populations are more likely to experience higher morbidity.
